summary: This is a medical bill that contains an illegal 'surprise' charge for out-of-network anesthesia and several other predatory billing errors, including duplicate and unbundled charges. The document is not legally sound because it admits to providing no prior notice for out-of-network care. The most important next step is to dispute the out-of-network anesthesia charge immediately.

red_flags.what: Out-of-network anesthesia charge without prior notice
red_flags.why: The bill explicitly states that no prior written notice was given for the out-of-network provider, which is a violation of federal law designed to protect patients from 'surprise' bills.

red_flags.what: Duplicate charge for Complete Blood Count (CPT 85025)
red_flags.why: The same lab test is billed twice on the same day, and the bill even includes a note stating it is a duplicate.
Calcium (82310) and Glucose (82947) were billed as separate charges, even though the bill notes they are already included in the Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (80053) that was also charged.

The provider billed a Level 5 visit, which is the highest and most expensive level of complexity, for an office visit associated with an appendectomy. This is often used to inflate costs when a lower-level code would be more appropriate.
The patient is being charged both a physician fee (99215) and a facility fee (G0463) for the same visit without prior disclosure, which is a predatory practice to increase the total bill.

your_rights: Under the No Surprises Act (42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111), you are protected from surprise medical bills when you receive emergency care or certain non-emergency care from out-of-network providers at an in-network facility. You also have the right to request a fully itemized bill and to dispute any charges that appear duplicate or incorrect under state consumer protection laws.
action_steps: Do not pay the bill in full until these discrepancies are resolved.

Call the Riverside General Hospital billing department and formally dispute the anesthesia charge, citing the No Surprises Act (42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111) and the bill's own admission that no prior notice was provided.
Demand the removal of the duplicate charge for the Complete Blood Count (CPT 85025) as noted on the statement.
Request a correction for 'unbundling' by removing the separate charges for Calcium and Glucose since they are already part of the Metabolic Panel.
Ask the billing department to provide the medical records used to justify the Level 5 (CPT 99215) coding for the office visit to ensure it was not upcoded.
caveat: The red flag categorized as Illegal should be researched further or discussed with a legal professional before taking action, as specific laws and protections can vary by state and individual situation.
